# Postshow

> Postshow is a closed-beta product by Eventools LLC (https://eventools.io). It is being built to connect product behavior to affected accounts and revenue, prepare product and customer interventions for human review, and check whether the outcome improved.

Key facts:

- Open core: the web app, CLI (npm package `postshow`), MCP server, desktop menu-bar agent, and the whole engine are MIT licensed. The always-on hosted cloud runtime and billing are the paid product.
- Pricing: Planned beta pricing is $0 with your own model API keys or local models via Ollama, $99/month for hosted Solo, and $249/month for hosted Team. Access is gated and there is no public checkout yet; final invitations and order terms control availability and limits.
- Models: user-selectable per task class (session watching, recon, deep dives, drafting) with per-task effort levels. Supported providers: Anthropic, OpenAI, Moonshot (Kimi), Z.ai (GLM), DeepSeek, xAI (Grok), Mistral, any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and local models through Ollama.
- Product focus: PostHog supplies behavior evidence, Stripe supplies account and revenue context, GitHub supplies code context, and Sentry can add error evidence. Other connectors are listed only when they have a tested gather or explicitly authorized destination path.
- Local-only: supported source credentials and raw source records stay off Postshow cloud. Postgres is always device-only and uses one owner-configured, bounded read-only SELECT; remote databases must require TLS. Its source rows may enter the evidence packet sent to the selected local or BYOK model on that device. Only schema-validated derived findings sync to Postshow, but those findings can still contain customer context. Ollama keeps model processing on-device; a remote BYOK model receives the evidence packet directly from the device.
- Setup: No supported npm release has shipped yet. Clone the GitHub repository, run `pnpm install` and `pnpm --filter postshow build`, then start setup with `node packages/postshow-cli/dist/index.js init`. Setup requires a provisioned workspace token and never places a secret in a model prompt.
- The agent plans its own work (nightly session sweeps, weekly deep dives, standing investigations) on a schedule the human can edit or veto.
